result.summary: The Social Security Administration says you were overpaid $6,240.00 in disability benefits between March 2025 and October 2025. This happened because you worked and earned too much money after your trial work period ended. You need to pay this money back. You have options to appeal this decision or ask for a waiver if you can't afford to pay.
result.reason: Our records show that you worked and earned $1,850 per month starting March 2025. These earnings exceeded the substantial gainful activity amount after your trial work period ended. We did not reduce your benefits for these months.

keyDates.label: Estimated date you received the letter
keyDates.note: SSA assumes you received the letter 5 days after the date on it.

keyDates.label: Deadline to refund full amount or contact SSA to avoid benefit withholding
keyDates.note: This is 30 days from the estimated receipt date. If you don't act, SSA will start withholding your full monthly benefit in December 2026.

keyDates.label: Deadline to request reconsideration to prevent benefit withholding
keyDates.note: This is 30 days from the estimated receipt date. If you ask within this timeframe, SSA will not withhold benefits until a decision is made on your appeal.

keyDates.label: Deadline to request reconsideration (appeal)
keyDates.note: This is 60 days from the estimated receipt date. You must verify all deadlines with SSA and on the notice.

keyDates.label: Benefit withholding starts
keyDates.note: If you do not refund the full amount or contact SSA within 30 days of receiving the notice, they will start withholding your full monthly benefit of $1,412.00.

options.name: Request reconsideration (appeal)
options.whenItFits: You believe the overpayment amount is wrong, or you were not overpaid at all. You must request this within 60 days of receiving the notice.
options.deadlineNote: You have 60 days from the date you received the letter to ask for reconsideration. If you ask within 30 days, SSA will not withhold your benefits until they decide. Verify this deadline with SSA and on the notice.

options.name: Request a waiver
options.whenItFits: You agree you were overpaid but believe it was not your fault AND you cannot afford to pay it back, or it would be unfair for you to pay it back. You can ask for a waiver at any time.
options.deadlineNote: You can ask for a waiver at any time. However, acting quickly can prevent benefit withholding. Verify this information with SSA and on the notice.

options.name: Ask for a payment plan / lower withholding
options.whenItFits: You agree you were overpaid and can pay it back, but not all at once, or you need a lower monthly withholding amount. This is an option if reconsideration or waiver is denied or not applicable.
options.deadlineNote: There is no specific deadline mentioned for requesting a payment plan, but it's best to contact SSA as soon as possible to discuss options and prevent full benefit withholding. Verify this information with SSA and on the notice.

result.recommendedReason: The notice states the overpayment was due to earnings exceeding the substantial gainful activity amount after your trial work period ended. It's important to ensure SSA has accurate information about your work dates, earnings, and the end of your trial work period. Reconsideration allows you to challenge the basis of the overpayment. If you also cannot afford to pay it back, you can request a waiver as a secondary option or at the same time.

I am writing to request a reconsideration of the overpayment notice I received, dated September 22, 2026. The notice states that I was overpaid $6,240.00 in Social Security disability benefits for the period of March 2025 through October 2025.

I am requesting reconsideration because I believe the overpayment amount is incorrect or that I was not overpaid as stated. The notice indicates the overpayment was due to earnings exceeding the substantial gainful activity amount after my trial work period ended. I would like to provide additional information or clarify my work activity and earnings during the specified period to ensure the accuracy of your records.

I understand that by filing this request within 30 days of receiving the notice, my benefits should not be withheld while the reconsideration is being processed. I received the notice on or about September 27, 2026.

I have attached a completed Form SSA-561, Request for Reconsideration, as required. Please review my case and notify me of your decision.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,

MARGARET L. OKAFOR
